title: Minimum Length of String After Operations
summary: Given a string s , you can repeatedly remove pairs of identical characters that are adjacent to the same character at an index.
statement: Given a string s , you can repeatedly remove pairs of identical characters that are adjacent to the same character at an index. The process involves selecting an index where the character on both sides is the same, then deleting the nearest matching character to the left and the nearest matching character to the right. The goal is to determine the minimum length of the string that can be achieved after performing these operations any number of times.
constraints: Choose a center character that has the same character somewhere on both sides.
Delete the nearest matching character on each side while keeping the center.
Return the minimum length after any number of operations.
hints: Each operation removes two copies of one character, preserving its count parity.
A positive odd count can be reduced to one; a positive even count can be reduced to two.
Sum one for odd frequencies and two for even frequencies.
Available centers permit these pair deletions independently for each character until the parity minimum remains.
editorial: Available centers permit these pair deletions independently for each character until the parity minimum remains.
